864: Theorem 4.8 .
865: Given a bigrassmannian v=v_{r,s,t,n} in type A_{n-1} with \mathfrak{S}_{v}=s_{i^{j}}, let
866: \displaystyle a
867: \displaystyle:=\min(n-r-i,r-j)
868: \displaystyle b
869: \displaystyle:=\min(i,j).
870: Then J_{v} is generated as an ideal of
871: H^{\star}(G/P_{J},{\mathbb{Z}})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r} by
872: (4.5)
873: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^{b},i^{j-b})\}.
874: Alternatively, J_{v} is generated by
875: (4.6)
876: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^{j},b^{a})\}.
877: We delay our proof of Theorem 4.8 until Section 4.7 .
878: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets ( 4.5 ) and ( 4.6 ) for J_{v},
879: the shapes \mu indexing the generators s_{\mu} run through an interval between
880: the j\times i rectangular shape i^{j} and the disjoint union of i^{j} with a
881: smaller rectangle of shape a\times b or b\times a.
882: In ( 4.5 ) the smaller rectangle is to the right
883: of the rectangle i^{j}, with both top-justified, while in ( 4.6 ) the
884: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle i^{j}, with both left-justified.
885: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size \binom{a+b}{a}
886: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
887: have generating function
888: \sum_{\mu}q^{|\mu|}=q^{ij}\left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
889: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q},
890: where \left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
891: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q} is a q- binomial coefficient or Gaussian polynomial
892: [ M91 , I.2 Exer. 3] .

claims.text: St. Dizier–Yong formulate Littlewood–Richardson coefficient linear systems under \(r<n\), \(a+j\le r\), \(a+i\le n-r\), \(b\le i,j\), and define “valid” tuples by these conditions plus \(N\le ab\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 270-303]

Their Algorithm 1 repeatedly applies a coproduct-based reduction to tensors representing those linear forms; it terminates because nontrivial updates strictly lower the degree of the left tensor factor. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 494-516]

The resulting argument proves tall linear forms lie in the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of wide forms in the bounded-\(N\) regime, then proves inconsistency of the relevant syzygy system. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 743-775]

743: \begin{lemma}
744: \label{lem:tall-dependent-on-wide}
745: Let $\varphi=(n,r,i,j,a,b,N)$ be valid with $N\leq \min(j,n-r-i)$. Then
746: $\linear_{\varphi}(\nu)\in W$
747: for any tall $\nu\in \decomp_{\varphi}$.
748: \end{lemma}
749: \begin{proof}
750: It is enough to show the analogous statement for tensors:
751: \[\mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_{\nu_B}\otimes \overline{s}_{\nu_R})\in \mathrm{Span}_{\mathbb{Z}}\left\{\mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_{\rho_B}\otimes \overline{s}_{\rho_R})\mid \rho\in\decomp_{\varphi} \text{ is wide} \right\} = T(W).\]
752: From $\varphi$ and $\nu$, suppose Algorithm~1 produced $\xi^{(0)},\ldots,\xi^{(K)}= \mathrm{Reduce}_{\varphi}(\nu)$. Then
753: \begin{align*}
754: \mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_{\nu_B}\otimes \overline{s}_{\nu_R})&=\xi^{(0)}\\
755: &=\xi^{(K)} -\sum_{m=1}^K (\xi^{(m)}-\xi^{(m-1)})
756: \end{align*}
757: By Proposition \ref{prop:hopf-identity-application},
758: \[\xi^{(K)}= (-1)^{|\nu_B|+1}(1\otimes \overline{s}_{(\nu_B)'}).\]
759: We have $\nu_B'\subseteq (b^a)'=a^b$. Since $a+i\leq n-r$ and $b\leq j$, it follows that $\xi^{(K)}\in T(W)$.
760: It remains to show that each term $(\xi^{(m)}-\xi^{(m-1)})\in T(W)$. By definition,
761: \[\xi^{(m)}-\xi^{(m-1)} = -\gamma\mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_{\lambda}\otimes (\overline{s}_{\mu^{(1)}}\cdots \overline{s}_{\mu^{(k)}})) \]
762: for some $\gamma\in \mathbb{Z}$ and partitions $\lambda,\mu^{(1)},\ldots,\mu^{(k)}$.
763: One observes from Algorithm~1 that \[|\lambda|+|\mu^{(1)}|+\cdots+|\mu^{(k)}|=N.\]
764: Since we are assuming $N\leq \min(j,n-r-i)$,
765: \[ \prod_{p=1}^k \overline{s}_{\mu^{(p)}}\in \mathrm{Span}_\mathbb{Z}\left\{\overline{s}_\theta\mid \theta\subseteq (n-r-i)^j\right\},\]
766: say
767: \[\prod_{p=1}^k \overline{s}_{\mu^{(p)}} = \sum_{\substack{\theta\subseteq (n-r-i)^j \\|\theta|=N-|\lambda|}} d_{\theta}\overline{s}_{\theta}. \]
768: Then if we expand, we obtain
769: \begin{align*}
770: \xi^{(m)}-\xi^{(m-1)}
771: &=-\gamma\mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_{\lambda}\otimes (\overline{s}_{\mu^{(1)}}\cdots \overline{s}_{\mu^{(k)}}))\\
772: &=-\gamma\mathrm{CP}\biggr(\overline{s}_{\lambda}\otimes \sum_{\substack{\theta\subseteq (n-r-i)^j \\|\theta|=N-|\lambda|}} d_{\theta}\overline{s}_{\theta} \biggr)\\
773: &=-\gamma \sum_{\substack{\theta\subseteq (n-r-i)^j \\|\theta|=N-|\lambda|}} d_{\theta}\mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_{\lambda}\otimes \overline{s}_{\theta}).
774: \end{align*}
775: Since $\lambda\subseteq \nu_B \subseteq b^a)$, each term $\mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_{\lambda}\otimes \overline{s}_{\theta})$ is of the form $\mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_{\rho_B}\otimes \overline{s}_{\rho_R})$ with $\rho\in\decomp_{\varphi}$ wide, it follows that $\xi^{(m)}-\xi^{(m-1)} \in T(W)$.
